# Full benchmark tables

<!-- Generated by scripts/make_leaderboard.py from results/results_regression.csv and results/results_event.csv; do not edit by hand. -->

One section per forecast length (3 h, 6 h, 12 h, 24 h) and one table per track. Each cell is the mean of a model's runs at that forecast length over the 5 folds and the 3 input lengths (1-day, 3-day and 7-day look-back, seq_len 288, 864 and 2016); forecast lengths are never averaged together. Runs with an undefined value are left out of the mean. `k/n` marks a cell where only k of the n runs of that forecast length (folds x input lengths) have a value, and † marks a model with fewer runs than that, whose rows are not directly comparable with the others (see the note under the section). RMSE (log10 flux) and MSA (median symmetric accuracy, %) are better lower; logR (correlation of the log10 values), HSS and TSS are better higher. HSS and TSS are per-day scores (one forecast per 24 h) at the M-class (SXR) and 10 pfu (proton) thresholds. Rows are ordered by the first channel's RMSE. Per-run results: [`results_regression.csv`](results_regression.csv), [`results_event.csv`](results_event.csv). Definitions: [`docs/metrics.md`](../docs/metrics.md).
